research_rationale: EO 12076 (signed 1978-08-18; 43 FR 37161-37162, Federal Register of August 22, 1978) was read in full in the held govinfo text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12076.txt (PDF pages 15-16; heading Executive Order 12076 of August 18, 1978, subject Levels IV and V of the Executive Schedule; number, date and subject agree with the census register row). Its authority is Section 5317 of Title 5. Section 1-101 places 17 positions, items (a) to (q), in level IV of the Executive Schedule; section 1-102 places 14 positions, items (a) to (n), in level V; section 1-201 provides that nothing in the order terminates or otherwise affects the appointment of the occupant of a listed position who held it immediately before the order's issuance; and section 1-202 revokes Executive Order No. 11861, as amended. The order has no sunset, termination, condition or report clause. The dossier's three own-terms leads (two condition leads and one fixed-term lead) were read in the source-ladder text and come from other documents printed on neighbouring Federal Register pages (the public-inspection notice, the list of rules going into effect and a Governors' proclamation), not from the order. The preamble recites the authority and the purpose (to place two positions in level IV and to codify other positions) and commands nothing beyond the sections. Whole-order end: EO 12154 (signed 1979-09-04; 44 FR 51965, Federal Register of September 6, 1979; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12154.txt, PDF page 9) section 1-202 states 'Executive Order No. 12076, as amended, is hereby revoked.' It has no effective-date or delayed-effect wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing. Later amendments, recorded as events and not ends under the owner ruling on strike-and-insert amendments (2026-10-21): EO 12099 (1978-11-17) deletes item 1-102(e), Director of Policy Review, Department of Defense, and inserts it as item (r) of section 1-101; EO 12111 (1979-01-02) deletes item 1-102(g), Assistant to the Secretary and Land Utilization Adviser, Department of the Interior, and inserts item (s), Counselor on Labor Management Relations, Department of Commerce, in section 1-101; EO 12119 (1979-02-14) deletes item 1-101(f), Assistant Attorney General, United States Attorneys and Trial Advocacy, Department of Justice, and inserts in lieu the Counselor on Legislative and Intergovernmental Policy, Department of the Treasury. Each moves or replaces a position, so the substance of those items changed; a human reviewer should note that. Clause 1-202 revoked EO 11861 once, on issuance; its first end is that performance. All other clauses ended with the order on 1979-09-04. The U.S. Code note under 5 U.S.C. 5317 held in jobs/theophilus-sources states that EO 12076, as amended by EO 12099, EO 12111 and EO 12119, 'was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 12154, Sept. 4, 1979, 44 F.R. 51965', which agrees with the date and instrument. The quarantined relationship lead naming EO 12060 is explained in the conflict resolution.
savings_reason: Read EO 12076 and EO 12154 for savings or continuing effects. The revocation of EO 11861 by EO 12076 section 1-202 persists after EO 12076 is itself revoked, and appointments made under EO 12076 are not undone by its revocation; EO 12154 re-lists eight of the positions in levels IV and V and its section 1-201 protects their incumbents. These consequences accrued or were carried forward and do not keep EO 12076 operative after 1979-09-04. The placements of positions EO 12154 does not re-list ended with EO 12076; no held source shows another instrument placing them.
conflict_resolutions: {"QUARANTINED_RELATIONSHIP_CONFLICT": "The Stage 19 causal queue lists five relationship leads for EO 12076. Four are read in full in held Federal Register texts: the amendments by EO 12099 (1978-11-17), EO 12111 (1979-01-02) and EO 12119 (1979-02-14) and the revocation by EO 12154 (1979-09-04). The fifth, an 'amendment' by EO 12060, is quarantined by the queue itself with the code PREDECESSOR_NOT_EARLIER_THAN_ACTOR, and the held note under 5 U.S.C. 5317 dates EO 12060 to May 15, 1978, before EO 12076 was signed on August 18, 1978, so it cannot amend EO 12076; no held text of EO 12076 or of a later order cites EO 12060 as affecting EO 12076."}
earlier_end_check: Searched on 2026-11-25 every held order text for the number 12076 (held texts of EO 12099, EO 12111, EO 12119 and EO 12154, the OFR 1989 codification copy of EO 12154, the source-ladder text of EO 12076 itself and the 5 U.S.C. 5317 note cite it; no other order does) and read EO 12099, EO 12111, EO 12119 and EO 12154 in full in the held Federal Register texts. No instrument revokes, supersedes or terminates EO 12076 or any whole clause before EO 12154 (1979-09-04). The three amendments strike or replace the wording of items and are recorded as later events; the only clause with an earlier end is 1-202, which was performed on issuance. Nothing in the order sets a date, condition or report that could end a position placement earlier. The machine USC, eCFR and OFR catalog searches record no other instrument; the one quarantined lead (EO 12060) is explained in the conflict resolution.
scope_check: The revocation by EO 12154 section 1-202 is of the whole order 'as amended', with no exception, so it reaches every position placement of sections 1-101 and 1-102 and the proviso of section 1-201. EO 12154's own section 1-201 protects incumbents of the positions EO 12154 lists and does not keep any EO 12076 provision in force. EO 12099, EO 12111 and EO 12119 each change identified items only; no held instrument amends sections 1-201 or 1-202.
independent_command_check: Sections 1-101 and 1-102 are 31 separate placements of one position each in level IV or V, each ending with the order; they are not independent of it. Section 1-201 is a rule of construction on the order itself ('Nothing in this Order shall be deemed to terminate' an incumbent's appointment) and has no operation after the order is revoked. Section 1-202 is a one-time revocation of EO 11861 performed on issuance, so its first end is 1978-08-18 and the revocation of EO 11861 persists as a surviving effect.
savings_check: EO 12154 section 1-201 preserves, for the positions EO 12154 itself lists, the appointment of the occupant immediately before its issuance, and EO 12154 lists again eight of EO 12076's positions (in level IV: Senior Adviser to the Secretary, Department of State; Deputy Under Secretary for International Labor Affairs; Administrator, Alcohol, Drug Abuse and Mental Health Administration; Special Assistant to the Special Representative for Trade Negotiations; in level V: Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Reserve Affairs; Executive Director, Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation; Executive Assistant and Counselor to the Secretary of Labor; Commissioner on Aging). Appointments made while EO 12076 was in force are not undone by its revocation; the placements EO 12154 does not re-list lapse with EO 12076, and no held source places those positions elsewhere or shows another placement.

research_rationale: EO 12121 (signed 1979-02-26; 44 FR 11195, Federal Register of February 28, 1979) was read in full in the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12121.txt (PDF page 19; heading Executive Order 12121 of February 26, 1979, subject Energy Coordinating Committee; number, date and subject agree with the census register row). It is one amendment: Section 1-102 of Executive Order No. 12083 of September 27, 1978 is amended by adding in alphabetical order item (x), the Director of the Community Services Administration, and item (y), the Chairman of the Council on Wage and Price Stability, to the membership of the Energy Coordinating Committee. It has no own-terms end, condition, report clause or sunset. The parent order EO 12083 (held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12083.txt, 43 FR 44813, Federal Register of September 29, 1978) was read in full: it establishes the Committee to coordinate Federal energy policy, lists its members in section 1-102, creates an Executive Council, revokes EO 11814, and contains no sunset, termination or report clause. First end: EO 12379 (signed 1982-08-17; 47 FR 36099, Federal Register of August 19, 1982; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12379.txt, PDF pages 9-10), section 20, revokes Executive Order No. 12083 'as amended', establishing the Energy Coordinating Committee. EO 12379 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing. The reason this revocation ends the command of EO 12121 (and is not merely a later formal disposition): EO 12121 acts only by amending a list inside EO 12083, EO 12083 has no sunset and so stayed in force, with its list as amended, until revoked, and section 20 revokes EO 12083 'as amended', which is EO 12083 including the additions made by EO 12121. EO 12379 names EO 12083 and not EO 12121 by number; the alternative reading, that an amendment not named by number survives the revocation of the order it amends, leaves a list inside a revoked order with nothing to operate on. Earlier ends tested and not found: EO 12379 recites that it terminates the establishing authorities of committees that are 'inactive or no longer necessary', but inactivity is not a legal end of EO 12083, which commands no performance by a date; no held instrument revokes, supersedes or amends EO 12083 or EO 12121 before 1982-08-17 other than the two amendments below; no held source dates any abolition of the Committee or of the Council on Wage and Price Stability, and the claim does not rely on one. Later events recorded, none an end: EO 12148 section 5-211 (signed 1979-07-20) adds item (x), the Director of the Federal Emergency Management Agency, to section 1-102 of EO 12083 without mentioning EO 12121, and EO 12156 section 1-101 (signed 1979-09-10; 44 FR 53073) corrects that item to read as a further amendment of EO 12083, as amended by EO 12121, adding item (z). EO 12288 (1981-01-29) revokes EO 12092 and does not mention EO 12083 or EO 12121. The U.S. Code, eCFR and OFR catalog machine searches were read for coverage; they record no other instrument affecting this order.
savings_reason: Read EO 12121 and EO 12379 for savings or continuing effects: EO 12121 states none, and EO 12379 section 20 revokes EO 12083 as amended with no savings or transfer wording. The amendment only enlarged a committee's membership and created no right, fund, property or appointment that outlasts the Committee, so nothing keeps the order operative after 1982-08-17.
earlier_end_check: Searched on 2026-11-25 every held order text for the numbers 12121 and 12083 (held texts of EO 12148, EO 12156 and EO 12379 cite them; no other order does) and the held Federal Register texts of EO 12083, EO 12121, EO 12148, EO 12156, EO 12288 and EO 12379 were read for the parts that touch the Committee. Nothing revokes, supersedes or terminates EO 12083 or the Committee before EO 12379 section 20 (1982-08-17). The census-register checks and the three machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, OFR catalog) record no earlier instrument. EO 12379's recital that it removes committees that are 'inactive or no longer necessary' is a reason for the cleanup, not a date on which the Committee lost legal effect.
scope_check: EO 12121 has one operative paragraph: the addition of items (x) and (y) to section 1-102 of EO 12083. There is no partial revocation, limitation or exception of that paragraph in a held instrument; EO 12148 and EO 12156 add a different member, item (z), by separate amendments.
independent_command_check: The only command of EO 12121 is the amendment of the membership list of EO 12083; the recital of the order's purpose, to enlarge the membership of the Energy Coordinating Committee, states its purpose and commands nothing. The command has no operation independent of EO 12083, so no independent command outlasts the revocation of EO 12083.
savings_check: Read EO 12121 and EO 12379 for savings or continuing effects: EO 12121 states none, and EO 12379 contains no savings clause for the Energy Coordinating Committee; the order gave the added officials a seat on a committee and created no right, fund, property or appointment that outlasts the Committee.
